findings.finding: Codex adapter is MVP-blocking (§18.1 step 7) but the PRD §25 demo launches ONLY a Claude Code session — there is zero Codex in any of the 17 demo steps. Codex is simultaneously the single most technically risky component in the whole plan (RISKS Top-5 #3 TR-02: app-server 'partly experimental', no settable session id → cwd+thread_id association race, no context-window %; plus TR-08 0644 world-readable rollout #21660). The draft is shipping a full second harness — with a CI schema-pin/regen pipeline (OQ-HARN-SPIKE-4) and a hardening pass — that the credible-demo goal does not exercise at all. This is the largest single overbuild in the MVP slice and the draft's own handoff explicitly flags it unresolved.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.1 step 7 'Codex adapter (app-server) — parity path (MVP-blocking per user)'; PRD §25 steps 1-17 reference only 'a Claude Code session' (step 6) — Codex never appears; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF line 74-75 explicitly lists as adversarial target: 'Codex parity claims — is app-server stable enough to be MVP-blocking, or should Codex be P1 with exec --json as the MVP stopgap?' and 'Whether both-harnesses-MVP-blocking + detached-daemon-day-one overloads the MVP slice'; RISKS.md Top-5 #3 (TR-02), TR-08; PRD §10.3 HARN-3 says 'MVP SHOULD support Codex CLI sessions IF FEASIBLE. If not, Codex support may be P1 but the data model must support it from the beginning.' — i.e. the PRD itself permits Codex-as-P1.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §18.1 (MVP technical slice) and §9.1 (harness adapter layer): keep the HarnessAdapter CONTRACT and the data model fully Codex-ready (PRD HARN-3 requires this) but DEFER the working Codex app-server adapter to P1. Demo on Claude only. Reframe step 7 from 'parity path (MVP-blocking)' to 'P1 — adapter contract proven Codex-ready in MVP via a contract-conformance test; live Codex adapter is the first P1 deliverable.' Document the criterion (demo proves the contract is harness-agnostic with one harness; second harness validates the seam in P1). This removes the riskiest CI/schema/hardening surface from the critical path without weakening the architecture.

findings.finding: The Brain PR-action-plan beat (demo steps 14-16 / §18.1 step 11) pulls a PRD-designated P1 capability into the MVP. PRD §16 lists 'Project Brain action plans through Action Gateway' under P1, and OQ-BR-4 lists 'propose-action-plan tools' as an OPEN (not resolved) MVP-blocking question with a 'read/query only, no proposals' fallback. The draft's MVP requires Brain to PROPOSE a multi-step PR action plan (a write-path proposal tool with preview/approve), which is materially more than the PRD §15 MVP line ('Project Brain drawer, read-only + draft/action-plan preview'). The PR itself could be created by a direct UI 'Create PR' intent (PRD §9.10, which is a first-class user flow) — routing PR creation THROUGH a Brain-proposed plan is a demo flourish, not a thesis-critical capability.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.1 step 11 'Project Brain drawer (read + propose a PR action plan; evidence chips) → approve via Gateway'; PRD §25 steps 14-16 'User asks Brain to create a PR / Brain proposes an action plan / User approves'; PRD §16 (P1 scope) explicitly lists 'Project Brain action plans through Action Gateway'; PRD §15 MVP must-have is narrower: 'Project Brain drawer, read-only + draft/action-plan preview'; OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-BR-4 status OPEN with fallback 'Read/query only, no proposals'; PRD §9.10 (Create PR flow) is a direct user action not requiring Brain.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §18.1 and §8 (user flows): split the Brain beat. MVP-blocking = Brain READ + evidence chips (demo steps 12-13, the actual differentiator) + a single-action 'propose PR' card as the minimal action-plan-preview surface (one ActionRequest, not a bundled multi-step plan). Make full multi-step bundled Brain action PLANS (AG §28.2 bundled plans / step-by-step approval) P1 per PRD §16. Confirm with human whether demo step 14-16 must be Brain-driven or whether a direct UI Create-PR intent (PRD §9.10) satisfies the demo while Brain-proposed-PR-plan moves to P1.

findings.finding: The MVP Action Gateway action-type set (§18.1 step 2 cites '~20 MVP action types', AG §28.2 lists 21) is roughly 3x what the PRD §25 demo path exercises. The demo needs ~7: project add/detect, create_worktree, session.create, approve/deny mutation, git.diff (review), brain.ask, github.create_pr_draft. Action types like linear.create_issue, review.request_agent_fix, session.pause, session.resume, brain.sync, brain.summarize_session, workflow.command.invoke, plan.link_task, linear.link_issue are not on the demo path and several map to deferred features (review.request_agent_fix = PR-checks-to-agent flow, explicitly P1 per PRD §16 and §18.2; linear.create_issue = one-way Linear sync, P1 per PRD §16/TASK-7). Building, risk-classifying, preview/dry-running, and testing 21 executors is meaningful work beyond a credible first demo.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.1 step 2 'the ~20 MVP action types (AG §28.2)'; ACTION_GATEWAY §28.2 enumerates 21 types including 'review.request_agent_fix' and 'linear.create_issue'; PRD §16 lists 'PR checks + agent fix flows' and 'One-way Linear creation from plan tasks' as P1; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.2 explicitly defers 'PR checks + agent-fix flow' and 'one-way/bidirectional Linear sync'; OQ-GW-4 status OPEN with fallback 'Trim to PRD §25 demo steps only'.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §18.1 / §6 (gateway module): define a tiered executor set. Tier-0 (demo-critical, MVP-blocking) = the ~7-9 executors on the PRD §25 path. Tier-1 (MVP-nice / P1) = the rest. Explicitly move review.request_agent_fix and linear.create_issue OUT of the MVP executor set to align with §18.2's own deferrals (they are listed as deferred elsewhere but appear in the MVP action list — an internal inconsistency). Resolve OQ-GW-4 to the demo-driven set.

findings.finding: Session survival scope is overbuilt for a credible demo. ADR-002 (detached daemon) is LOCKED and not relitigated — but the SURVIVAL POLICY built on it (ADR-010 resume-or-replay, serialized scrollback VT replay, lossy alt-screen re-attach) is the #1 critical risk in the entire register (TR-01, the 'genuine risk cluster', hardest correctness problem), and the PRD §25 demo never restarts the daemon. The draft's own RISKS open-question #1 asks whether MVP survival should be scoped to replay-only. Full resume-or-replay-with-VT-serialization for alt-screen TUIs is a large, fragile workstream that the demo does not require and that risks sinking the slice into terminal-fidelity QA.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §3 ADR-010 / §12 'resume-or-replay on daemon restart'; RISKS.md Top-5 #1 TR-01 'critical / high', 'the genuinely fragile part', 'accurate re-attach of the TUIs ... is the hardest correctness problem'; RISKS.md open question #1 'Is MVP survival live-across-full-quit or resume-or-replay-and-relaunch? Pin the exact guarantee'; CLAUDE_CODE_HANDOFF line 73 'is resume-or-replay the right policy, or should MVP scope to replay-only?'; PRD §25 has no daemon-restart step.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §12 / §Session Lifecycle: keep detached-daemon-day-one (LOCKED) and UI-restart→reconnect-live (cheap, demo-relevant), but scope MVP daemon-restart survival to REPLAY-ONLY + relaunch with an explicit 'restored view, process relaunched' banner (the ADR-010 fallback). Defer harness --resume integration and accurate alt-screen VT re-render to P1. This removes the hardest QA correctness problem from the MVP critical path while preserving the architecture and the survival seam.

findings.finding: Internal inconsistency: the draft simultaneously claims 'macOS-only is the MVP target, optimize for credible demoable MVP over a calendar deadline' AND loads the MVP slice with two harnesses, a notarized bundled Python sidecar (the 'sharpest packaging risk' / release-blocker, TR-04/OQ-PLAT-SPIKE-1), resume-or-replay survival (TR-01), and a 21-action gateway. The §18.1 build order is presented as 'the smallest vertical that proves the thesis' but several steps (Codex parity, full Brain action plans) exceed the thesis-proving demo. The draft does not reconcile its stated scope discipline (PR-01 mitigation: 'build the locked seams only ... Cut to Claude-Code-only adapter + read-only Brain for first demo') with the §18.1 contents that contradict that very fallback.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT preamble line 5 'optimize for a credible, demoable MVP slice (the PRD §25 scenario) over a calendar deadline'; RISKS.md PR-01 mitigation/fallback 'Cut to Claude-Code-only adapter + read-only Brain for first demo (PRD §25)' — this is the draft's OWN documented scope-cut, yet §18.1 builds the opposite; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.1 header '[LOCKED]' on a slice the handoff says is still being pressure-tested.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §18.1: change the slice tag from [LOCKED] to reflect the finalize decision, and reconcile it with the PR-01 fallback the draft already endorses. Adopt the draft's own stated scope-cut (Claude-only adapter + read+single-propose Brain) as the MVP, and move Codex-adapter + full-Brain-plans + resume-survival to a clearly tagged 'P1 / first-fast-follow' block. State the scope-discipline rule once and make §18.1 obey it.

findings.finding: Workflow/cc-crew scope in MVP is appropriately limited to DETECTION (good — matches PRD §15 'Workflow Pack detection states / cc-crew detection at least' and §18.2 defers personalization/team/TDD-tracker), but the MVP action set still includes workflow.command.invoke and plan.link_task, and the workflow module (§6) lists 'command registry; cc-crew parsers (plan/architecture-anchor); personalization runs as Gateway action plans.' Personalization-as-action-plan is correctly deferred in §18.2, but the demo only needs cc-crew DETECTION (PRD §25 step 3 'detects ... cc-crew workflow signals') and plan-task selection (step 5). command-invoke and full parser machinery exceed the demo.
findings.evidence: PRD §25 step 3 'Platform detects git repo, Project Brain state, and cc-crew workflow signals' (detection only) and step 5 'opens Plan View and selects a plan task'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6 workflow module includes command registry + personalization; ACTION_GATEWAY §28.2 includes 'workflow.command.invoke'; PRD §15 MVP 'cc-crew detection at least' (detection, not invocation); ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.2 defers full personalization/upgrade UI.
findings.proposed_fix: In ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§18.1: scope MVP workflow module to detection + advisory readiness + plan-file parse-for-selection only. Drop workflow.command.invoke from the MVP executor set (it implies running pack commands, which needs personalization the demo doesn't have). Keep it P1. This is a minor trim that tightens the slice to the demo's detection-only requirement.
